evidence.note: Earlier revision of the paper under scan, authored by Barry Revzin. R2 concedes the R0/R1 mechanism for naming base classes entirely, keeping only designators for direct or indirect non-static data members, and says naming base class subobjects can be done later; across the arc to R6 the base-class naming syntax stays dropped and non-designated initializers for base class subobjects (B{{.a=1}, .b=2}) are added instead.
evidence.quote: This revision eschews that approach entirely: it’s simpler to just stick with naming members, direct and indirect.
evidence.speaker: author
evidence.title: P2287R2: Designated-initializers for Base Classes

evidence.note: In a std-proposals thread on P2287R4, Jens Maurer replies to a commenter who wants "::" instead of "." for naming base classes, saying the paper is mostly design-complete and EWG-approved and that anyone proposing a departure from its status quo must convince the paper's authors — i.e. he defends the paper's existing design against the alternative.
evidence.quote: The paper is mostly design-complete and EWG-approved; with just a small question open from CWG.
evidence.speaker: other
evidence.title: Re: [std-proposals] P2287R4 Designated initializers for Base Classes - Double Colon

evidence.note: The compare page shows brevzin's Clang branch p2287 with six commits by brevzin (Sep 8 and Oct 27, 2024) implementing the paper's facility: diagnosing non-designated initializers that follow designated ones, synthesizing InitListExpr to handle indirect members, and fixing inheritance and lookup. It is the author's own prototype implementation of P2287 in Clang.
evidence.speaker: author
evidence.title: Comparing llvm:main...brevzin:p2287 · llvm/llvm-project
